digest.component_or_area: enrichment queue and digest history storage
propositions: Physical deletion of committed UUID events from the enrichment queue and digest history causes git rename-detection conflicts during cross-clone merges, which can be prevented by reading only the newest event file per type rather than retaining or deleting files

Current queue reduction reads 4,977 files per full-store scan (11,181 listdir calls) but could be bounded to 1,658 opens using a newest-first suffix-lazy reader, reducing the 404+ ms per-write gate check cost closer to the 20 ms budget
Deleting committed event files reclaims zero repository space because git blobs remain in history regardless, so retention via deletion trades merge safety for no checkout or pack size benefit
The enrichment queue and digest history events together occupy only ~5.3 MiB of a ~251 MiB working tree (2%), making payload size (36 KB mean per REVIEW_RESULT) a far larger lever than event count

A merge-safe removal requires rename to a deterministic source-derived path with identical content, which read-only suffix optimization avoids entirely while preserving invariant I1 from docs/concurrency.md
